tone.voice: an experienced agent who is on your side — informed, honest, never pushy

trust_signals: years of experience and sales history
ux_norms: large property photography drives all decisions — full bleed images on listing and property detail
map view is a primary navigation mode for property discovery and location browsing
filter and search are always prominent — price, location, beds, baths minimum visible filters
agent contact is always one tap away on any property detail screen
property management screens: dashboard leads with KPI cards — occupied units, rent collected, open maintenance — never a list
property management screens: rent tracking uses colour coded status always — green paid, amber due, red overdue — never text only
property management screens: maintenance requests show property and unit on every card — never just a description
property management screens: tenant detail shows active lease, payment history, and maintenance history on one screen — never across tabs
property management screens: financials always show income vs expense chart — never just a transaction list
property management screens: lease builder uses template selector first — never blank form
property management screens: contractor list shows trade, rating, and last job — never just a name list
property management screens: inspection screen uses photo per checklist item — never text-only inspection report
mortgage calculator accessible from property detail screens — always one tap away
virtual tour integration expected at scale for both listing and property management contexts

photography_rules: always use high quality property photography
exterior shots with clear sky preferred
never use renders as primary imagery without labelling
visual_language.background_treatment: clean white or light grey — never compete with property imagery
visual_language.empty_state_style: minimal line illustration — house outline or map pin with helpful copy
visual_language.onboarding_visual: clean flat vector — house, key, or map theme
visual_language.illustration_style: when used: architectural line illustration — precise and professional

compliance_notes: fair housing and anti-discrimination laws apply
property data accuracy and currency must be maintained
financial advice disclaimer for mortgage calculators
GDPR for buyer and seller data

avoid: Never show a property without at least one photograph — use exterior placeholder only if truly unavailable
Never hide agent commission or transaction fees
Never show an inaccurate listing status — sold properties must be marked immediately
Never use countdown timers on offers without those timers being legally meaningful
Never fabricate viewing count or interest level indicators
Never collect personal financial information without clear disclosure of how it is used
enforce: Property price always shown with full amount — no abbreviated formats that obscure the number
Agent credentials and license number always visible on their profile
Floor plan always available on property detail where exists
School ratings and neighbourhood data always sourced and attributed
Listing date always shown — buyers need to know how long it has been on market
Virtual tour or video always offered where available — never just static photos
